growth.juvenile_note: No juvenile form: single glassy, boat-shaped diatom cells divide every few days and link into ribbon- or tree-like colonies in the brine channels at the underside of sea ice. By spring they stain the bottom few centimetres of the ice golden-brown, then are released into the water as the ice melts; a few cells overwinter in the ice to seed next year's bloom.
growth.source: Arctic sea-ice algae literature (N. frigida is the key colonial pennate diatom of bottom-ice communities; spring bloom roughly Mar-Jun when light returns, growth at <1% of surface light, released at ice melt); values are for the visible bloom layer
